title-group.article-title: MAPT knockdown and neuronal survival in a test dementia model

abstract.p: Tau accumulation is a feature of the test dementia model. Knockdown of MAPT raised neuronal survival by 32% relative to a scrambled control (p < 0.01).

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: The test dementia model accumulates tau in cortical neurons. Earlier work in this model measured survival over 7 days.
This study extends the window to 14 days and adds a scrambled control.

sec.title: Cell culture
sec.p: iPSC-derived cortical neurons were kept in Test Medium at 37 degrees C.

sec.title: Knockdown
sec.p: An antisense oligonucleotide against MAPT was added at 5 uM for 14 days. The scrambled control used the same dose.

sec.title: Results
sec.p: Knockdown of MAPT raised neuronal survival by 32% relative to a scrambled control (p < 0.01). Survival was measured by live-cell imaging on day 14.

caption.p: Neuronal survival on day 14 for MAPT knockdown and scrambled control.

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: The survival gain matches the 7 day result and holds at 14 days.

sec.title: Conclusions
sec.p: MAPT knockdown protects cortical neurons in the test dementia model.

app.title: Appendix A
app.p: Oligonucleotide sequences are listed in the supplementary file.
